predecessors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Ravenna 'with its port and environs, north to the Po and south to the Marecchia', the Pentapolis, and 'a group of duchies including Rome, Venetia, Calabria, Naples, Perugia, and Lucania', 'mainly the…

successors.name: Lombards
successors.text: Aistulf 'captured Ravenna and all the provinces subject to the Exarchate' (Aistulf page, dated 750 there, 751 on the Exarchate page); the Pentapolis follows in 752

successors.name: Papal States
successors.text: the territories 'belonging to Ravenna' given to the pope in the 756 treaty: Forli with its hinterland, Lombard conquests in Romagna and the Pentapolis (Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia, Ancona)

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: infobox 'Succeeded by' lists the Republic of Venice; the lagoon duchy of 'Venetia'

ledger.x: 584: the Byzantines set up an exarch at Ravenna.
641: Rothari takes the last imperial land of the Veneto mainland.
728: Liutprand gives Sutri to the papacy.
740: the Pentapolis is again listed with the Exarchate.
740: Rome drops out of the Exarchate's list.

wars.name: Lombard invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: The Lombards under Alboin took Milan (569) and Pavia (572, after a three-year siege), split into duchies after Alboin's murder (573), and killed the imperial general Baduarius in 576; Tiberius II reorganised what was left into five provinces in 580 and the…

wars.name: Rothari's conquest of Liguria and the lower Po
wars.outcome: Rothari took the Ligurian coast, 'all the cities of the Romans' from Luna westward, and the remaining imperial land of the lower Po valley including Oderzo in 641; the exarch Plato's counter-invasion was beaten on the Scultenna near Modena in 645 with the…

wars.name: Liutprand's war with the Exarchate
wars.outcome: Liutprand took Bologna, Osimo, Ancona, Rimini, the Pentapolis, Emilia and Classe in 727 but not Ravenna; Sutri went to the pope in 728; Venetians expelled the Lombards from Ravenna after 731; by 740 the Pentapolis is listed with the Exarchate again.

wars.name: Aistulf's conquest of Ravenna and the Frankish intervention
wars.outcome: Aistulf took Ravenna (751; 750 on the Aistulf page) and the Pentapolis (752); Pepin forced him to return Roman lands in 755 and again in 756, after Aistulf's second siege of Rome, and the 756 treaty gave the Exarchate's territories to the pope.

certainty.note: The Exarchate was a string of coastal cities and corridors between Lombard lands; no treaty line survives.
